title: On the Spread of a Virus and Traveling Waves, Part I
summary: This paper develops a one-dimensional model for a mobile viral component propagating through a spatially distributed susceptible population. Random viral motion produces diffusion, whereas a response to the relative gradient of susceptible density generates directed transport. The existence of a positive entire traveling wave is proved when directed transport dominates diffusion, and the limiting case of equal transport and diffusion coefficients is constructed separately.
